role: The Discord surface onto KGSM — a channel per server, live status, and authorized commands from chat.

fields.label: Log level
fields.description: Minimum severity this leaf logs.

fields.label: Bot token
fields.description: Token the bot signs in to Discord with. Without a valid one it cannot connect at all.

fields.label: Discord server id
fields.description: The Discord server this bot operates in. Pointing it at another server abandons the channels it made in this one.

fields.label: Action role id
fields.description: Role whose holders may start, stop and otherwise act on servers from Discord — the same role the assistant checks. Zero means no one is authorized.

fields.label: Channel category id
fields.description: Category the bot creates each server's channel under. Zero leaves new channels uncategorised.

fields.label: Delete channel with the server
fields.description: Whether uninstalling a server also deletes its Discord channel, taking that channel's history with it. Off, the channel is left behind.

fields.label: Running marker
fields.description: Shown beside a server that is running.

fields.label: Stopped marker
fields.description: Shown beside a server that is stopped.

fields.label: Uninstalled marker
fields.description: Shown beside a server that is no longer installed.

fields.label: Clean up status messages
fields.description: Whether status messages are removed after a while, so a busy channel does not fill with them.

fields.label: Status message lifetime
fields.description: How long a status message stays before it is removed.

fields.label: KGSM executable
fields.description: Path to the KGSM executable. Everything the bot knows about this host's servers is read through it.

fields.label: KGSM event journal
fields.description: Directory holding the engine's event journal, which the bot reads so a channel's status updates the moment a server starts or stops. Read-only and shared with every other consumer — nothing needs configuring on the engine side.

fields.label: Watchdog socket
fields.description: The supervisor's control socket, which the bot starts and stops servers through.

fields.label: Server list cache
fields.description: How long the list of servers is reused before being re-read from KGSM.

fields.label: Blueprint cache
fields.description: How long the blueprint catalog is reused before being re-read from KGSM.

fields.label: Ollama endpoint
fields.description: Where the language model is served from. Unreachable, the bot still reports status and runs commands but cannot answer questions.

fields.label: Model
fields.description: Name of the model to run, as Ollama knows it. It has to be pulled on the endpoint above and has to support tool calling.

fields.label: Context window
fields.description: How many tokens of context the model is given. Larger holds more conversation at once and costs more memory on the machine serving the model.

fields.label: Model timeout
fields.description: How long to wait for the model to finish a response before giving up on it.

fields.label: Temperature
fields.description: How much the model varies its wording. Low keeps answers consistent and literal, which is what tool calling wants; high makes them more inventive.

fields.label: Sampling seed
fields.description: Fixes the model's randomness so the same question gives the same answer. Leave it unset for normal use.

fields.label: Thinking mode
fields.description: Asks the model to reason before answering, on models that support it. Slower, and only worth it for a model trained for it.

fields.label: Conversation database
fields.description: File holding past conversations, which is the bot's memory between messages. Pointing it elsewhere starts an empty history and leaves the old one behind.

fields.label: Maximum tool steps
fields.description: How many times the bot may call a tool while working on one message before it has to answer with what it has.

fields.label: Tool output limit
fields.description: How much of a tool's output the model is shown. Truncating keeps a long listing from crowding out the conversation.

fields.label: Step-limit reply
fields.description: What the bot says when it hits the tool-step limit without reaching an answer.
fields.default: I wasn't able to finish that after a few steps — could you rephrase or break it down?
